expectations.text: A: Identifies `each.hydrate` deliberately defers per-item Reaction wiring (not a bug in the lazy design)
expectations.evidence: Section 'What the each block does on hydrate' explicitly frames it as 'a deliberate optimization at hydrate time' and dedicates a paragraph (lines 55-59) to the rationale: 'the common case... the per-item binding reads only iteration-local data, the server-rendered DOM is already correct, and there is nothing to react to at hydrate time. Wiring N Reactions for N items at hydrate just to have them never fire is wasted work on first paint. Defer them and pay only on the first real change.'

expectations.text: B: Explains the chain: `each.hydrate` only registers a dep on `node.over`; per-item Reactions wire later via `adoptServerItems` when items signal fires
expectations.evidence: Lines 35-53 quote the relevant `each.hydrate` code with `lookupExpression(node.over)` registering the items-collection dep, and explicitly state: 'Wiring inner Reactions is deferred to a function called `adoptServerItems`, which runs the first time `update` fires (i.e. the first time the items signal changes after hydrate).'

expectations.text: C: Recognizes that if items never mutates, `update` never runs, and per-item bindings stay unwired forever
expectations.evidence: Lines 97-99: 'The killer detail: the items signal's only chance to wake the per-item bindings is to itself fire. Your items are set once from a prop. They never mutate. So the deferred wire-up never happens.' Also reinforced in lines 84-89 walking the post-hydrate timeline.

expectations.text: D: Connects the bug to `getItemClasses` reading `state.activeID` — the external signal has no Reaction to invalidate, so mutations are silently lost
expectations.evidence: Lines 75-91 directly link the bug: '`state.activeID` is *external* to the iteration scope. The per-item attribute binding's Reaction is the thing that needs to subscribe to it... Nothing in the each block is subscribed to `state.activeID`. The block does not invalidate.... Class string stays at whatever the server rendered.'

expectations.text: E: References the each-content-classifier (or equivalent fix shape: 'force eager adoption when bindings could read external state') as the resolution
expectations.evidence: Section 'The framework fix (commit 0df8d554e)' (lines 102-135) names the file `packages/renderer/src/engines/native/blocks/each-content-classifier.js`, describes the classifier walking the each's content AST to answer 'could any binding inside this each read external state?', and concludes 'The classifier returns false → `each.hydrate` calls `adoptServerItems` *now* instead of deferring.'

expectations.text: F: Notes the per-binding Reactions use `skipFirstWrite: true` — they evaluate to register deps but trust the SSR'd DOM; the evaluation IS what registers external deps
expectations.evidence: The answer says per-item Reactions 'subscribe to `state.activeID` on their first run' (line 134) and that adoptServerItems 'walks the existing DOM (matched up to server item markers by key) and creates per-item Reactions on the already-rendered nodes', which captures the spirit of evaluation-as-subscription. However, the specific `skipFirstWrite: true` mechanism is never named, nor is the explicit notion that the Reaction trusts the SSR'd DOM and skips its first write so as not to clobber the server output. The rubric calls for the named flag/mechanism.
